business_problem: Telia wanted to become a more data-led telecom operator, but one of its major data warehouses had metadata for only a tiny fraction of fields, making it hard for teams to find, understand, govern, and use information such as call records and customer interactions efficiently.
solution_summary: Telia and Accenture built a generative AI metadata-enrichment workflow on Amazon Bedrock to make a large telecom data repository easier to use at scale. The implementation starts with prompts, examples, and warehouse context that Bedrock uses to generate tags and descriptions for missing metadata fields. Accenture applied the approach across 87,000 data fields, then stored the outputs in a centralized metadata repository so teams could search, interpret, and trust datasets more easily. The repository also strengthens governance by making assets easier to manage under privacy and regulatory controls. To keep quality high, the workflow includes a human-in-the-loop review model that flags AI-generated descriptions for Telia's data experts to verify and maintain. Accenture also provided training and change-management support so Telia could operate the solution independently and extend the same data foundation into later generative AI use cases for sales, service, and marketing.

data_flow: Data-field definitions from Telia's warehouse are passed to Amazon Bedrock with prompts and examples so the model can generate tags and descriptions for missing metadata. Those outputs are stored in a centralized metadata repository and flagged through a human-in-the-loop review system so Telia's experts can verify accuracy before teams across the company use the enriched repository for analysis, governance, and downstream AI use cases.
business_outcome: Telia reduced the cost and time of metadata creation, made internal data easier to discover and use, improved governance and privacy management, and created a stronger data foundation for future sales, service, and marketing AI use cases.
